title: The Good Shepherd
review_status: DRAFT: retelling and wondering questions require theological and editorial review before release.

source.note: Original child-friendly retelling written for this prototype; not a quotation of any translation. Follows the shape of the Good Shepherd presentation used with young children: the sheep are known and called by name, they know the shepherd's voice, and he leads them out to pasture. See also Psalm 23.

formation_themes: being known and called by name

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Jesus once said something very important about himself, using a picture of a shepherd and his sheep. Let's carry the material to the table, and listen.

segments.text: Jesus told about a shepherd and his sheep. At night, the sheep rest safely inside the sheepfold.
In the morning, the shepherd comes to the gate of the sheepfold. Jesus said, "I am the Good Shepherd."
The Good Shepherd knows each one of his sheep. He calls his own sheep by name.
And the sheep know his voice. When they hear him calling, they come to him.
He leads them out. He walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
He brings them to green pasture and fresh water, where they have everything they need.
Jesus said, "I know my own, and my own know me." The Good Shepherd loves his sheep so much that he gives his life for them.

wonderings: I wonder who the Good Shepherd is.
I wonder who the sheep might be.
I wonder how it feels to hear someone call your name.
I wonder how the sheep know the shepherd's voice.
I wonder what the green pasture is like.

steps.prompt: When you're ready, return each figure to its place in the box.

feedback.mismatch: That place is shaped for a different figure.
feedback.all_good: Each figure is resting in its place.

outro.speaker: narrator
outro.text: The material is back on the shelf. It will be here whenever you want to return to it.

journal_line: I listened to Jesus' words about the Good Shepherd, who knows each of his sheep and calls them by name.
